page.layout: One text column; in the right margin, beside the lines "exarsit, ut Caesarem" to "Galliae", a small marginal note. Running head at top. Catchword "quan-" at right below the last line.

main_text.p: omnium dignitatem & splendorem obfuscauit, Illustrissimo PRINCIPI VLADISLAO dicare non est veritus: Egone Responsum meum, quo Principum honor a tam alto despectu, pro viribus, vindicatur, dignissimo PRINCIPI CAROLO inscribere, & illo magnifico nomine munire reformidarem? Aut quum Ille, in Epistola Dedicatoria, Principem suum ad funesta bella gerenda accenderet: ut non Ego potius BEATE-PACIFICI Regis filium (quoad fieri potest) ad pacem inter Christianos colendam fouendamque impensius adhorter? Tempora ipsa loquantur, Templa Pacis semper magis gloriosa & diuturna, quam trophaea Victoriae. Paci vero hostis capitalior nullus, quam spiritus ille, qui, Religionis ergo Turcae propensior quam nominis Christi Professoribus, tanto odio in Principes Protestantes exarsit, ut Caesarem, & GalliaeThuan. hist. Anno 1551. pag. 473. de Iubo[?] III. Pont. Regem incusaret, quod illi cum Protestantibus amicitiam conclusissent,

page.notes: Running head "NVNCVPATORIA" read as printed. Margin note read as "Timan. hist." in the scan; most likely "Thuan." (de Thou); "Iubo" also doubtful, as is the Roman numeral. Scan is faint in places; the italic/roman boundaries in the first lines follow the visible typeface and may be imprecise. No page number is printed. The word "quam" at the end of the page is followed by a flourish-like mark; read as "quam" without a hyphen.
